definitions: to shine (intransitive), to shine on/to brighten (transitive), to shine X on Y (*adazalle X yl ni Y*, ofc this usage is transitive). to explode, to burst, to be tangy. Pairs with **nevu**
to kill, to be deadly (yt)
to remember to do something (yt). Pairs with **patwaen**
to extend your legs straight, to stretch your legs, to stand on your toes
to bend your legs such that a sharp acute angle is formed (yt)
to reach for something by standing on your toes or stretching your legs (yt)
to wrinkle your nose, to sniffle (yt)
to peck with a nose (uk)
to gift, to give
to smell, to inhale through the nose. See also **pwaivu** and **aivumuz**
(from **aivu**) to smell hesitantly, to inhale through your nose slightly (as when sleeping)
to sweat
to stretch out your whole body

to do something by stretching out your whole body (for example, said of animals looking big to scare off predators, said of basketball players being defensive, said of tennis players diving to get a ball) (yt)

to teach (a person), from stative **asdi** (uk). For the topic, use kjask/kjawel/vaeli or ni or ve. Hmm, I can't decide what makes the most sense. Or should I even use ael? Anyway, for example *asdilaentu ojovu ve ni sa* "I will teach you how to swim". Actually, maybe just *asdilaentu ni ojovu sa (okae)* would make sense….
to sneeze. Note: formerly *asuzu*
to close (as in, "the door closes" (compare with **jemla**)), to finish (intransitive). Can also be used to describe a sunset, as in *atla ynti*.
to close (as in, "I closed the door" (compare with **jemlaen**)), to finish/to complete (an action) (uk) (transitive). Note: has ael/il contrast
to abandon, to leave behind (intentionally)
to measure, to assess (uk). For example, "How can one measure the sun's heat?" *ko damaen kworr mutko yl ni ynta yntig wa*
to take care of, to nurture (uk)

to find after searching. As an example "It took me 2 whole hours to find a satisfactory door/For the better part of two hours, I searched and then found a useful door" – *kwygytaenku devu siz tul pynak ni memak zwez*
to drink (yt)
to drink a bit of a drink, to sip, to try a drink (yt)
to do chores, to do errands, to do daily work

to forget, to lose (as in to not have something anymore), to leave an object (unintentionally) (yt)

to sleep, to live or reside somewhere, to be from somewhere (yt). Also see **mjaztela**.
to nap, to have a short sleep (yt)
to save (as in not pay money), to do something that makes you still have__, to keep (guardar)
to die. Note: used often with tem.
to make excited, from stative **gagmo** (uk)
to form, to appear (transitive) (uk). For example, *sarrgav ni tomak kworraega tae, poitjeza* "Form a single-file line, kids"
to form, to appear (intransitive). For example, *gavjokla tomak poitjega tae* "A single-file line of kids was formed"
to open (as in, the result of this verb is that something is more accessible (as in more physically accessible or usable, usually)) (intransitive)

to open (as in, the result of this verb is that something is more accessible (as in more physically accessible or usable, usually)) (transitive) (uk). Can be used for example, unlocking a door (where as with jakti, that would be opening a door, which would gepytaen a room or house or whatever). To ask someone out, to ask out. to coach, to train
to buy
to spend money

to decide (transitive) (uk)
to do something or act nice/kind (can also be to do a favor, or to volunteer) (uk). Can be used causatively (pg 94/95), with the sense of helping.
to be dangerous, to harm (uk). Compare to **lumailaen**.
to gather, to make ready, to prepare. (uk) Note: see **ilaemaen te**.
to block, to get in the way
to describe, **pwinevu** is to clarify
same as **mazaen**, but with sight (uk)
to listen, to hear (yt). Compare to **twalle**
to breastfeed (human or animal)
to lie (as in not tell the truth). Note: has ael/il contrast
to push (yt). Also used in causitive constructions, with the flavor of intentionality and by strong force. Note: has ael/il contrast
to extend your arms straight, to reach out with your arms (intransitive)
to bend your arms such that a sharp acute angle is formed (yt)
to reach with your arms for something, to strive for something (transitive) (yt)
to open (as in, "the door opens" (compare with **gepytla**)), to start (instransitive), to use. Can also be used to describe a sunrise, as in *jaktla ynti*
to open (as in, "I opened the door" (compare with **gepytaen**)), to start (transitive), to use. Note: has ael/il contrast
to choose something specific (yt). Note: *jarraen ni X ni Y* means "to choose both X and Y". Also can mean to point at, or to pick out or single out something. Emphasis on the thing chosen.

to choose between Y and Z, where an optional X contains Y and Z, as in *jarrvu X ael ni Y ni Z*. For example, *jarrvu ice cream ael ni chocolate ni vanilla* "To choose between chocolate and vanilla ice cream". Also can mean to point at (elaborate?). Emphasis between the possible options or the option not chosen (for example, jarrvytuku ni chocolate instead of vanilla)   Note: has ael/il contrast
to house/keep/have pets/animals. For example, *jazaikitu ni dyvym* "I have a mouse (as a pet)"
to daydream, to picture while thinking, to think and wander, to imagine
to dance (yt).
to close (as in, the result of this verb is that something is less accessible (as in more physically accessible or usable, usually)) (intransitive).

to close (as in, the result of this verb is that something is less accessible or usable (as in more physically accessible, usually)), to cover, to decline someone asking you out (transitive) (yt). Can be used for example, locking a door (where as with atlaen, that would be closing a door, which would jemlaen a room or house or whatever). Also used in causitive constructions, with the flavor of being the negative conjugation of **gepytaen**. So, can't use negation with **jemlaen** in this usage.
to breathe, to show a sign of life, to be born
to choke, to drown (yt)
to delay, to procrastinate
to cough (yt). So, *jetwerrken* would mean to give a single cough.
to shout at, to argue at, to berate loudly (yt)
to shout, to yell, to raise your voice (often *jetwvaenuz*), to bark (dog) (yt)
to hold back, to stifle (in general, to hold back something when it would be easier or more natural to do it), to 'help it' (as in 'I can't help it' *jevu okaego* )

to win (note that what you win will be the object an ael phrase), to beat, to surpass, to catch up (yt). For example, *jezytaenku tjez ael ni sa* "I beat you in chess", *jezytaenkik kworrjygpae jempwag ni 9000000000* "the world population hasn't surpassed 9,000,000,000", *jezaenugk u ni sa okaega. ta wirrmusk pynil tjewkitas* "I can't catch up to you–you run too quickly". Note: has ael/il contrast
to collect, to gather, to bring, to amass. Note: subject is non-human and object is a bunch of the same item or a bunch of different items. Compare to **ykalle**

to improve (yt). Can also be used causitively. Can also mean to become a better __ or to become better at __, the structure is **jolkaen ni __ (tem)**. For example, "I got better at swimming" *jolkytaenku ni ojovu*.
to fall to/towards (yt). Note: has ael/il contrast. Compare with **kisla**
to realize, to notice, to note, to observe, to spot (uk)
to find, to come across, to meet someone unexpectedly.
to trip. Note that **jupelamuz** means to lose your footing, and **jujupela** means to trip and fall/crash. Note: has ael/il contrast. For example, *jupejoklu kezy ael* "I tripped on the rock"

to count, to list, to order (food at a restaurant or tickets at a theatre, etc.), to tell someone a small bit of pre-packaged info like a phone number or a short google search result (yt). Note: count from X to Y \= jygaen X kja Y ve
to swallow (intransitive), to come to a decision (after hard deliberation)
to mistaken X for Y, to think X is Y (mistakingly), *jyrraen X ael ni Y* (uk). Note: has ael/il contrast

to transition to stormy weather (such as the time before a thunderstorm when it's thundering but not raining) (yt)
to lightning (uk)
to grow (uk) (transitive). Also used in causitive constructions, with the flavor of intentionality and over the long term.
to confront, to challenge, to face
to grow (intransitive)
to release, to decompress, to release pressure from
to move by use of some machine, to drive, to bike, etc. Can mean you operate it or someone else does. (yt)

to light (fire, candle), to turn on (light, tv/phone), to make something bright using glass (like with a magnifying glass), to shine (flashlight, torch, lantern), to 'start something that has high energy' (such as a party, an animated conversation, an argument, etc.) (uk)
to snow (yt)
to gesture to someone to come over
to drop (yt). Note: has ael/il contrast
to fall (from). Note: has ael/il contrast. Compare with **jotwaen**
to spill. Note: has ael/il contrast. Derived from *kis-*(from *kisaen*) \+ -*jo* \+ *-vu*

to work on, to do something with a bit of focus, with an implication of a bit of progess being made (yt). Examples are working on conlang, making a meal, working on a quest in a video game, working on homework.
to be when there's a full moon. Also to stay up all night, to pull an all-nighter.
to be when the moon is out with few clouds (uk)
to leave, to exit (yt) (intransitive). Note: has ael/il contrast. Compare to **kwaezla** and **tisaen**.
to continue backwards (with "mi"), or to turn around (yt)
to give a plan which is a summary, which hits the important points (yt)
to talk animatedly, to talk excitedly (yt)
to hide (transitive) (yt). Note that *kopunaen te* would mean to hide, intransitively
to attach (as in *korrovu X ael ni Y* "to attach Y to X"). Note: has ael/il contrast
the 'en' form kukjelena is used to mean 'shut up', as a more harsh way
to bite (something), to close (something) (atlaen or jemlaen) forcefully (yt)
to walk slowly/relaxedly
to arrive to a destination after a long journey/travel (uk). Pairs with **nondavu**.
to figure out, to think through, to reason it out, to think it out
to grind, to turn into crumbs/dust
to call, to get the attention of something (yt) (can use *yl* to express what words you use to get the attention), to call by name (use *yl* to denote the name), to call by phone
to leave, to exit (all to a wide, open space, like a forest or field) (intransitive). Note: has ael/il contrast. Compare to **kjajaen** and **tisaen**.
same as **mazaen**, but by sound (uk)
to shake, to mix, to consider something (transitive), to earthquake (yt)
to shake, to digest, to earthquake (intransitive)
to classify, to categorize (yt). For example, "what did the meteorologists classify that hurricane?" *ko kwesytaenki damu ni kalunjaerr rruv ni mutko*
to bloom

to dream, to dream about (both as in the sleep type of dream)
to show or to uncover (to make an object visible)

to change an object's position or appearance (yt)
to organize, to structure, to plan (yt)
to lay on your back. Same as **llakantaen**, but only used in certain dialects. Note: has ael/il contrast (?)
to lay on your back (uk). Same as **llakantaejela**, but only used in certain dialects. Note: has ael/il contrast (?)
to go a long distance, to try (put in good effort, no success is indicated or not indicated) (uk)
to grow hair, to have hair (uk)

to flip over, to reveal (make visible), to lend (prestar) (use ve or a purposive/preventative for whomever is being lent), to depend on (as in to be determined by, not to rely on) (X depends on Y \= loksaen Y ni X) (yt)
to meet, to approach, to meet up with, to see (to meet up with) (uk). Compare to **pwynarraen**
to sit (on your butt). Has ael/il contrast (?)

to (esp. suddenly) have an opinion, to think some thing may be true (more suddenly) (uk). Compare to stative **maz**, which does not have the connotation of 'suddenly'
to do nothing. Maybe in some dialects, it also has the meaning of **nwazalle**.
to bleed

general verb, used for unspecified actions or implied actions (yt). Often a translation for 'to do' or 'to go'. Also can mean 'to do things', 'to do activities'. Also used in causitive constructions, with the flavor of neutral/no intentionality or non-intentionality implied.

to laugh (yt)

to swim. Note: formerly *ojonu*

to act upon remembering to do something (uk). As in, "After remembering to do so, I went to cook a meal in the kitchen" – *patwukaenku ni zolytukaenku zolytug ael ni orrpae*. Pairs with **aijolaen**.

to make yourself useful, to help, to lend a hand (yt). Compare to **zamarr** and **vizarr**. See page 178 for more.
to look away fast

to close your eyes, to ignore. Ambitransitive
to eat (especially) tasty food or (less commonly) drink an especially tasty drink

to step, to step on (uk). Also used in causitive constructions, with the flavor of accidental causation of something small. Note that the effect was accidental, not necessarily the action that caused the effect. For example, *poitykenki kis u ni vilpae ni rrau turrtaekai* (should be *turrtaek*, with the updated changing stative endings) means that I may have dropped the book on accident or on purpose, but the effect of the cat getting a bit scared was accidental.
to climb slowly or shimmy (with feet and hands), to crawl (uk). Note: has ael/il contrast
to twitch, to squirm, to shake fast, to shiver (ditransitive)

to do (uk–used to be yt). Used with nouns/imperative verb phrases/adjectives  to refer to doing an activity involving said noun/verb phrase/adjective. As in, "I want to have breakfast" – *pukarraen orrvaty aetjykwig da u.* Can also mean to behave or act (like something) when used with il adverbs. Also can mean, 'went like/was like/goes like/is like', as in 'I was like, why did you go to that place??' *pukytarraenku kova atja muk ma loto ael sa* Some set expressions: 1. pukarraen jaimerr : to betray 2. pukarraen kaigepyt (ni patw) : to give a friendly hello (with body contact\!) 3. pukarraen kerryk : to shovel snow to the side, to make a pile of snow 4. pukarraen masavaty : to have dessert 5. pukarraen morrk: to grunt, to make unintelligible sounds with the mouth 6. pukarraen myk : to spend time with, to interact with, to be with (who you spend time with marked by mla), to talk to 7. pukarraen orrvaty aetjykwig/yntampeg/mystaegaeg : to have breakfast/lunch/dinner. Note that just pukarraen orrvaty would be more common, unless you want to emphasize having a meal at a certain time. 8. pukarraen pezal : to shower, to bathe, to get clean, to clean oneself 9. pukarraen pwa : to clean the house, to do chores, to get the house ready 10. pukarraen walempae : to do some work, to do work (alternative to walemaen) Can also be used to referring to a previous action in the utterance, as in	*urrkwytalleki ma ni semetaeska pukarr ilk*, literally "she complained about slowness, which she did slowly"(pointing out irony/hypocrisy).
to whisper

to marry

to be when it's equally parts cloudy and sunny (a bit leaning towards cloudy side) /partly cloudly

to be cloudy (looks like it might rain soon/soonish) (yt)

to crack (intransitive), to get wrinkles. **pwepwezla** : to shatter, to break up with (rough break up, compare with **talaen**)(used with *mla* for this sense)

to enter, to come, to go in, to come in, to get on (all to something kind of closed, like a pot of soup or a building, not like a forest or field. Can be used for a building or vehicle) (intransitive). Of course, has ael/il contrast. Compare to **sorrala**.
to put something inside somewhere, to insert. To fill X with Y could be pwipwivu X ael (ael) ni Y. Note: has ael/il contrast phrases: **pwivu (.... ael) ni pa** -\> to stare intently (at ….)
to catch (for example a ball), to snatch, to take the bait (a fish), to be affected by someone's words (usually in a negative context, in a 'you should just ignore it what they say' type way) (yt).
to pass/give/hand someone something small, to tell a (single) joke, to make a funny remark, to sell (something little, or a little). Note: has ael/il contrast. Compare to **malekzarr**.
to meet someone for the first time, to learn of someone (uk). Compare to **lopwataen**

to happen, to take place, to occur (uk). Note that **rrantaen Y ni X** means for X to experience or for X to live through Y. For example, *memok pak rraentukaenki kalunjaerr ni ja* "I've never experienced a hurricane before" (perhaps said while talking about the hurricane about to come)
to make someone/something like someone/something else, to get someone into something (uk). Example:  *rralukaenki ma ni ojovu u* "He got me into swimming". From stative **rra**
to have, to possess, to use, to grab (as in make yourself have, possess, use) (uk)
to travel
to do something early, to be early, to do something ahead of schedule (uk). Compare to **vutla**
to snore
to play seriously, to practice, to train
to get a result, to get a finished product, to end up with something (yt). Often the second verb in a serial verb phrase, for example: *ko kwesytaenki damu ni kalunjaerr rruv ni mutko*
to make something (X) appear as something else (Y) (yt). It's phrased like this–*sadaen X ael ni Y.* Note: has ael/il contrast ofc
